clue.text: More open as a poker player?

definitions.meaning: bluff as an adjective means frank and outspoken, so the comparative is more candid
someone at the card table who bets heavily on a weak hand to fool the others

explanation.surface: A question whether a card player is more candid than others, when the opposite is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective meaning hearty and frank, and also the noun for a card player who pretends to hold strong cards.

clue.text: Buxom little Maureen's turning into lad

indicators.note: into says the turned name goes inside the lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: turning says the short name and its S are read backwards

parts.note: Mo is a short form of Maureen, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Curvy little Maureen turns into a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' looks like a change of state for Maureen, but it is the reversal signal; 'into' places the result inside the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a woman with a large, full chest: buxom and well-endowed are near synonyms.

clue.text: Ready for service, nuns gambolled every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then takes every other letter of nuns gambolled, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Nuns, prepared for church, frolic from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit to be put to work or employed, which is being ready for service.

clue.text: Amicably finish with girl after 24 hours

indicators.note: after puts the finish and the girl behind the day

parts.note: a day of 24 hours, here Friday, abbreviated Fri
finish means end
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Breaking up with a girlfriend nicely a day later.
explanation.definitionFit: In a friendly, warm way: an adverb of manner synonymous with amicably.

clue.text: Regret eating extremely purgative Indian bread

indicators.note: eating says the regret word swallows the letters taken from purgative

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of purgative

explanation.surface: Someone regrets eating a strongly laxative Indian loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so 'Indian bread' is the currency, not naan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the rupee is India's currency unit.

clue.text: Stay with the wretched Daniel, say

parts.note: a stay is a support or prop

indicators.note: wretched suggests the word 'the' is in a sorry, mangled state

explanation.surface: An invitation to remain with the miserable Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is one of the Old Testament seers, an example of a biblical foreteller.

clue.text: Multi-faceted dons exercise and do legal work

indicators.note: dons means wears, so the faceted piece puts the exercise around itself

parts.note: PE is physical exercise
rose-cut describes a gem cut with many triangular facets

explanation.surface: Versatile university dons work out and also practise law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like academics but is the verb wear. A rose-cut diamond has many facets.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a case in a court of law against someone, a lawyer's or state's job.

clue.text: Curse love, a source of troubled hearts

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letters of troubled and hearts

explanation.surface: Damning love as the cause of broken hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or profanity; an expletive can be called a curse.

clue.text: They are frequent visitors, but he is a vagrant

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of but he is a roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Regulars, though one of them is a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulars who habitually go to a place such as a cafe or bar.

clue.text: Very French attempt to seduce is wrong, legally

parts.note: tres is the French word for very
to make a pass is to try to seduce someone

explanation.surface: A very French advance is against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort or wrongdoing, especially entering land without permission.

clue.text: Did butterfly, perhaps, lead to illumination for mystic?

parts.note: butterfly is a swimming stroke, so doing it is swimming in the past tense

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, here of illumination

explanation.surface: A question whether a butterfly's flight brought a holy man enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher, a spiritual master who seeks union with the divine.

clue.text: Kitty finally got fit in leisure facility

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money put in by several people

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word got

parts.note: fit means capable or able

explanation.surface: A cat at last got into shape at a sports centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A table for playing snooker-like games, a piece of recreational equipment in pubs and clubs.

clue.text: Mum and daughter collect underwear I dropped and put it on

indicators.note: Mum and daughter gather up the underwear between them, one at each side

parts.note: mum is mother, MA

indicators.note: dropped says the letter I is let fall from the underwear word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: A mother and daughter gather up underwear; one drops something and then puts on an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put it on' looks like dressing in the underwear, but it means faking; 'dropped' signals the lost I and 'collect' the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To put it on is an idiom for faking, here pretending to be ill to shirk duty.

clue.text: Blue-eyed boy's rebellious action

indicators.note: rebellious, revolting, suggests the favourite's letters turn over

parts.note: a blue-eyed boy is a favourite or pet, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A favoured lad does something defiant.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure or move taken, as in taking steps against something.

clue.text: Yankee puts on silly voice, regardless of what happens

indicators.note: puts on says the Yankee letter is dressed in the silly word

parts.note: silly means inane
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet
to vent is to voice feelings

explanation.surface: An American adopts a daft way of speaking come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning whatever the outcome, an idiom of the same sense.

clue.text: Actor representing genuine class

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters of genuine class are presented in another form

explanation.surface: A performer who plays genuine class on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: ALEC GUINNESS was a celebrated British actor, star of The Bridge on the River Kwai and Star Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Guinness was a famous English stage and film performer, so an example of the class.

clue.text: Arachne cries, seized by desire for surge of naughtiness

indicators.note: seized by says the setter's cry is held inside the desire word

parts.note: to crave is to desire
the setter, Arachne, refers to herself as I
mew is a cat's cry

explanation.surface: The setter weeps, gripped by a longing for a spell of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is the setter, so she is I, and her cry is MEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise in law-breaking, here wittily softened to mischief.

clue.text: Mescal made skipping maidens go up the wall

indicators.note: skipping says the maidens are passed over, removed

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so maidens are two Ms

explanation.surface: Mezcal drove some young women round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up the wall' looks like getting angry, but it is literal scaling.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb a fortress rampart with ladders, a literal scaling of a wall.

clue.text: Massive column with rope around

indicators.note: around says the rope word turns round

parts.note: a lasso is a rope with a noose

explanation.surface: A huge pillar with a rope wound round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like the rope encircling the column, but it signals the rope word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge or gigantic, a synonym for massive.

clue.text: Grasses break up topsoil at last, taking ages

indicators.note: break up tells us to smash the word topsoil into a new order
at last picks the final letter of the word taking

parts.note: ages are long periods, eons

explanation.surface: Lawn plants take a long time to break up the topsoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' is a verb here, not plants; 'break up' rearranges TOPSOIL into STOOLPI.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasses as a plural noun in slang means police informers, which is exactly what this decoy-bird term means.

clue.text: I hoard bananas in beehive, perhaps

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of I hoard go wild

explanation.surface: Someone stashes bananas in a beehive.
explanation.walkthrough: A beehive is a tall rounded 1960s hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: The beehive is an example of a styled coiffure.

clue.text: Worships alto and soprano after quarter of an octave

indicators.note: after places the octave fragment behind the alto letter

parts.note: A is the musical abbreviation for alto
an octave has eight notes, do re mi fa so la ti do; two of them make a quarter
S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: Choir singers giving praise after a bit of a scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol-fa names the scale's notes do, re, mi and so on; two notes, DO RE, are a quarter of eight. The alto A comes first, with S closing.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere or idolise, verbs in the third person like worships.

clue.text: Adolescent's first kiss touching a bit of a nerve

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Adolescent's

parts.note: X is the kiss written at the end of a letter
touching means on, against

explanation.surface: A teenager's first kiss strikes a nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long fibre of a nerve cell that carries impulses, so a part of a nerve.

clue.text: Stroke heads of beagles eagerly advancing in anticipation

indicators.note: advancing says those letters go forward, in front of the stroke
heads of takes the opening letters of beagles and eagerly

parts.note: a forehand is a tennis stroke

explanation.surface: Someone pats eager hounds as they surge forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like the verb pat; it is the tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in advance, ahead of time, is what in anticipation means as an adverb phrase.

clue.text: Scotsman's armpit bitten by fox terrier

indicators.note: bitten by says the word sits within the jaws of fox terrier

explanation.surface: A Scot is nipped under the arm by a terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern English dialect word for the armpit.

clue.text: Roots of St Ignatius Loyola, soldier and absolutist

indicators.note: in a down clue the roots of words are their bottoms, their last letters

explanation.surface: The origins of the Jesuit founder, a soldier and a hardliner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roots' looks like origins, but in a down clue it means the bottom letters of each word. Ignatius Loyola was indeed a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor was an autocrat with unlimited power.

clue.text: One helping Turkey and half of Uzbekistan start to thrive

parts.note: a turkey is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: half of takes the latter five letters of Uzbekistan
start to takes the opening letter of thrive

explanation.surface: An aid worker helps Turkey and part of Uzbekistan begin to prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country beside Uzbekistan; it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide, someone who gives support to another in their work.

clue.text: Conclusion of movie, Three Kings, skirting over inaccuracy

indicators.note: conclusion of takes the final letter of movie
skirting says the kings surround the over letter

parts.note: R stands for rex, king, so three kings are three Rs
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: The end of the film Three Kings skims over a factual slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake, a slip from what is correct, the same thing as an inaccuracy.

clue.text: Expand section of integral network retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says a stretch of letters lies within the words integral network

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to extend part of a vital network after the fact.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Expand section' as the definition, but 'section of' is the indicator for the hidden letters and 'Expand' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make bigger or extend, a straight synonym of expand.

clue.text: The Spanish shunning sex and food

indicators.note: shunning says the Spanish article is avoided, removed

parts.note: relations is a polite word for sex
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards avoiding sex and food, an odd austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed allowances of provisions, as handed out to soldiers, so food supplies.
